svg.text: How one request travels: client → security filters → method security → service → database. Red = where it can be stopped (HTTP code). Purple = what gets written to the security log.
One request through the security filters
SecurityFilterChain "apiSecurity": stateless JWT · CSRF off · CORS on
200 / 201 + ApiResponse JSON {success, status, message, data} — errors come back in the same JSON shape
no Bearer header → go on as anonymous
anything else → must be logged in
a rule on every protected method:
the user id comes from the
no token on a protected URL
role or owner rule says no
@Order(1) csrfDemoSecurity — only /csrf-demo/**: it keeps a session cookie, so CSRF tokens are ON;
a form sent without the hidden _csrf token → 403, logged ACCESS_DENIED reason=CSRF
@Order(2) apiSecurity — everything else: STATELESS (no session, no login cookie), CSRF OFF
(there is no cookie a forged page could use), CORS ON, JwtAuthenticationFilter,
AccessMonitorFilter, and oauth2Login only when Google keys are set (profile google)
Method security: @EnableMethodSecurity turns every @PreAuthorize into a check before the method runs
logout puts the jti on the blacklist until "exp"
HTTP status codes in this API
invalid body or parameter (strict JSON, validation)
not logged in, or a bad / expired / revoked token
logged in, but not allowed (role, owner, CSRF, CORS)
conflict: old version, duplicate, own ADMIN role
too many failed logins: wait (Retry-After header)
the login, token and access code has no logging calls: the aspect writes every line
2 add 1 to a counter in memory
WARN ACCESS_DENIED user=anna ip=10.0.0.4 method=GET path=/api/users reason=ROLE
(every line starts with the date and time)
the in-memory counters, since the last start
the report counters live in memory:
a restart sets them back to 0
the log files are the permanent record
Logging in, logging out and the in-memory stores (DSA)
tokens are not stored in the database: the server keeps only small maps
finds the user by email, or creates a READER
the token is in the #fragment: a browser
never sends it to any server
only this token: other devices keep theirs
role change · profile change · user deleted · admin DELETE …/sessions
→ every token of that user goes on the blacklist ▸ logged: TOKENS_REVOKED
O(1) check on every request; each entry
revoke all tokens of a user: one lookup
at the front of the deque
Three examples: who may do what
same filters for everyone; the token's roles and the owner checks decide
public: GET /api/posts/** is permitAll, no token needed
AUTHOR ben — manages his own posts
token roles: ["AUTHOR"] · owns post 12 · post 7 is claire's
hasAnyRole('AUTHOR', 'ADMIN'); author = uid from the token
the post is at version 1 now (optimistic locking)
Ownership: no such post (404 before "not yours")
his post → soft delete (row kept, deleted_at set)
token roles: ["ADMIN"] · his own id is 1
jti on the blacklist: log in again to get the new role
his own account: he can't drop his own ADMIN role
log user 5 out everywhere; returns the count
